content: Discontinuation refers to the cessation of a procedure and can have different implications depending on whether it pertains to the treatment of an individual or the discontinuation of an entire drug product line. 1. Discontinuation of a treatment involves stopping the use of a specific drug. This may occur for several reasons: The condition or ailment for which the drug was prescribed has resolved, rendering further use unnecessary. The adverse effects of the drug outweigh its therapeutic benefits, making continued use detrimental to the patient. Superior alternatives to the drug have become available, offering better efficacy or safety profiles. 2. Discontinuation of a drug product occurs when the manufacturing and/or support of the product is halted by the company responsible for its production. This is often due to declining sales, although it does not necessarily indicate that the product was never successful. Many drugs that were once high-selling eventually experience a reduction in demand and are discontinued, often after being replaced by a more advanced or effective product.
